analysis: Reviewed the two base_text units of desktop-app/package-lock.json (base lines 3958-5477). They are unchanged surrounding context: esbuild, escalade, got, glob, jsdom, lightningcss, lodash, node-gyp and similar entries. The changed ranges that fall inside this span are small: base 4044-4046 (fast-uri 3.1.8), 4474-4476 (http-cache-semantics 4.2.0), 5267-5269 (nanoid) and 5354-5356 (node-gyp's nested undici). The patch excerpt is truncated, but it shows the intended changes: electron 44.5.1 to 44.9.1, vite 8.3.2 to 8.3.5, @oxc-project/types 0.152.0 to 0.155.0, and rolldown binding bumps 1.2.12 to 1.2.15. Every entry in the supplied range points at registry.npmjs.org with sha512 integrity hashes, and the dev flags are preserved. The supplied range shows no new non-registry resolved URLs, no removed integrity fields, and no new install-script dependencies beyond the existing fsevents. This is a desktop-app dev-tooling lockfile update. It does not touch the provider process, the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011), key custody, the model or prompt data paths, or any other threat-model asset. I found no regression or invalidated assumption. Limits: the head side and the full patch were not supplied, so I could not verify the new integrity hashes or the remaining changed ranges (about base 5594-6685). The Electron bump is a security-relevant runtime dependency, but nothing in the supplied evidence suggests a regression. A final pass could confirm that all head-side resolved URLs are still registry.npmjs.org and that no lockfile entries were injected.
